g(h)=\frac{5}{h}sin⁡(\pi +2h).

From the graph, what is ${lim}_{h\to \,0}g(h)?$ If the limit does not exist, write "DNE" (without the quotation marks).

feedback.worked_solution:
The graph shows that as we approach $h=0$ from the left, the $y$ value approaches $-10.$ So, the left-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{h\to \,{0}^{-}}g(h)=-10.
$$

Similarly, when we approach $h=0$ from the right, the $y$ value approaches $-10.$ So, the right-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{h\to \,{0}^{+}}g(h)=-10.
$$

Since both the left and right-hand limits exist and are equal to $-10,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{h\to \,0}g(h)=-10.
$$
